turns.prompt_text: what is the difference between a string bean and a green bean
turns.response_html:
The terms string bean and green bean are generally interchangeable today, both referring to the young, edible pods of the common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris).

The name "string bean" originated because older varieties had a tough, fibrous string that ran along the seam of the pod, which had to be removed; most modern varieties are "stringless," but the old name persists. Green beans are also called snap beans because of the sound they make when snapped.
